senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. אנק) [to press,] (cmp. מָצַץ) to suck.
units: <cite ref="Sotah 12b:20">Sot. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>ולא י׳</he> and he (Moses) would not suck; <he>פה … יִנַק דבר טמא</he> shall the mouth destined to speak with Divinity suck in an unclean substance?—
Ber. 10ᵃ; a. fr.—Trnsf. to draw sap, absorb.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 71b:2">B. Bath. 71ᵇ</cite> <he>יוֹנְקִין משדה וכ׳</he> they (the plants) are nurtured from the consecrated field.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 3:5:4">Y. Erub. III, 21ᵇ</cite> <he>איברים יונקין זה מזה</he> the limbs of an animal draw nourishment from one another, i.e. in either portion of a slaughtered animal to be divided between two partners there are substances absorbed from the other; a. fr.

<cite ref="Pesachim 112a">Pes. 112ᵃ</cite> … <he>יותר לִינָק … להָנִיק</he> more than the calf desires to suck, does the cow desire to give suck, i.e. the teacher is more anxious to teach than the pupil to learn.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 7b:20">Bekh. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>כל המוליד מֵנִיק</he> every viviparous animal is a mammal.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 5:5">Keth. V, 5</cite> <he>ומֵנִיקָה את בנה וכ׳</he> (Y. ed. <he>ומֵינִ׳</he>) and she is bound to nurse her child herself.

<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 1:4">Nidd. I, 4</cite> <he>נתנה בנה למֵנִיקָה</he> (Y. <he>למינ׳</he>) if she gave her child out to a wet-nurse. Ib. 5 <he>ומניקה</he> and while she nurses a child. Tosef. ib. II, 2; <cite ref="Ketubot 60a:14">Keth. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>מֵינֶקֶת שמת וכ׳</he> a woman whose husband died during her nursing period.
<cite ref="Ketubot 65b">Ib. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>סתם מֵנִיקוֹת וכ׳</he> as a rule nursing women are of delicate health.
<cite ref="Taanit 27b:7">Taan. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>מניקות שיָנִיקוּ וכ׳</he> in behalf of the nursing women (they prayed) that they might be able to nurse &c.; a. fr.
